title: A separated etale algebraic space over a scheme is a scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $q:E\to X$ be a morphism. Assume that $q$ is etale in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $V\to E$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume also that its diagonal $E\to E\times_XE$ is a closed immersion, meaning that every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $E$ is represented by a scheme $Z$ over $X$, and $Z\to X$ is etale. No quasi-compactness assumption is made on $E$ or $q$.

source.place: Tag 03XU (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite) and Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), in Section Tag 0417 (section-schemehood).

proof.text: Let T be the terminal object (X,id) of Sch/X and f:E→h_T the unique natural transformation. Yoneda preserves terminal objects. For each chart a:h_V→E, its composite with f corresponds to the unique morphism V→T; its underlying scheme map is V.hom. Thus the chartwise etale hypothesis supplies the input to [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite], giving chartwise local quasi-finiteness. Identify the Yoneda equivalence with yoneda.preimage using yoneda.map_preimage.

Because h_T is terminal, the product E×E is a pullback of f along itself. The induced product-to-pullback isomorphism carries the absolute diagonal prod.lift(id,id) to pullback.diagonal f, by the two projection identities. For every scheme test a:h_V→E×_{h_T}E, apply the given [def-weil-closed-immersion] test to a followed by the inverse comparison isomorphism, and transport its representing pullback square through the comparison isomorphism. This gives exactly the diagonal hypothesis required in step 3, in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. No separate scheme-level properness or separatedness predicate is needed.

source.place: Separated morphisms and their diagonal; the algebraic-space testwise convention is the item definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] with base scheme S=X, target T=(X,id), algebraic space E and the unique map f. Steps 1 and 2 give its hypotheses. Obtain Z in Sch/X and e:h_Z≅E; its compatibility with T is automatic because T is terminal.

For every test a:h_V→E of the isomorphism e.hom:h_Z→E, take the representing scheme V, projection id_V and map a≫e.inv:h_V→h_Z. The resulting square is a pullback because both vertical maps are isomorphisms. Its underlying scheme projection is the identity, hence an open immersion and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). Thus e.hom is a representable etale chart in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the original chartwise hypothesis to e.hom to obtain Etale Z.hom [def-weil-etale-morphism], and pair it with the representing isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_of_separated_etale {X : Scheme.{u}} (E : AlgebraicSpace X) (het : ∀ (V : Over X) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ E.obj.obj), IsEtale a → Etale V.hom) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 E.obj.obj) (𝟙 E.obj.obj))) : ∃ Z : Over X, Nonempty (yoneda.obj Z ≅ E.obj.obj) ∧ Etale Z.hom
